cf-perfrel-cap: Confirm the maximum realistic performance uplift over baseline for this delivery organisation, and whether exceeding the published benchmark is credible here.
cf-perfuplift: Provide the reference throughput baseline (last 2 quarters) so the uplift denominator is measured rather than assumed.
cf-vtax-cap: Confirm the maximum share of engineering effort that can go to review before the delivery model becomes uneconomic.
cf-vtax-base: Provide the current review effort as a share of engineering time (timesheet or Jira extract).
cf-qual-cap: Confirm the accepted ceiling on rework attributable to AI-authored code quality.
cf-qualbar: Confirm how quality risk should weigh in the go/no-go decision.
cf-hri-floor: Confirm the minimum adoption a zero-readiness team would still achieve, based on a previous transformation.
cf-hri-slope: Provide the outcome of a comparable past change programme so readiness-to-adoption can be calibrated.
cf-supshare-cap: Confirm the maximum share of the retained team that may supervise rather than produce.
cf-supshare-fac: Confirm how supervision effort scales with the human-supervision matrix.
cf-glassfactor: Confirm the engagement context (fixed price / T&M / managed service) and its effect on achievable automation.
cf-rampcap: Confirm the maximum annual adoption the organisation can absorb.
cf-rampspeed: Confirm the realistic pace of adoption against comparable internal programmes.
cf-khmult: Provide the current collective-competence level and the target agreed with the client.
cf-autoposture: Confirm the product profile (new build / feature add / maintenance) and its share of the scope.
cf-ceiling: Validate, artefact by artefact, which deliverables require an irreducible human signature - ideally with the certification authority or quality function.
